title: The path of food through the gut
caption: Food passes from the mouth along the oesophagus to the stomach, the small intestine, the large intestine and the rectum. The liver, gall bladder and pancreas are accessory organs: food never passes through them, but they secrete into the small intestine. Most digestion and absorption of nutrients happens in the small intestine.
alt: Six boxes in order: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine and rectum; a separate box for the accessory organs (liver, gall bladder and pancreas) with a dashed arrow into the small intestine.
description: Mouth: teeth chew food; saliva contains amylase.
Stomach: churns food; secretes hydrochloric acid and pepsin.
Small intestine: the main site of digestion and absorption.
Large intestine: absorbs water and forms faeces; the rectum stores them.
Accessory organs (liver, gall bladder, pancreas): food does not pass through them.
